analysis: Supplied units are documentation only: changelog.d/large-memory-checkpoint-stage-cap.md (new, lines 1-9) and docs/reference/configuration.md (head line 508 row for DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_SSD_MAX_STAGE_MB/_MS, plus date bump at line 3). The PR claims complete-checkpoint SSD restores on Macs with >=96 GiB now default to a 3072 MiB / 2500 ms staging cap, up from 1024 / 1000. Explicit env values still win. Attention block caches are unchanged, and the daily write cap is unchanged. Under T-041 (e), staging is transient RAM under a shared GlobalKVCacheBudget reservation, with refusal falling back to recompute. The docs state that native destination plus scratch is reserved before allocation, so this is an availability/memory-pressure tuning change. It does not alter TTL, HMAC naming, AAD, cacheSalt scoping or the kill switch. Deeper restores (16k vs 8k tokens) somewhat widen the same-account TTFT hit/miss signal (SEC-035), but that risk is unchanged in kind. The actual implementation (provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/KVCacheSSD/SSDPrefixCachePolicy.swift) was not supplied. The next pass should verify that it: detects physical memory and applies the 96 GiB threshold; applies the larger cap only to complete checkpoints; keeps the larger read cap bounded by the GlobalKVCacheBudget reservation before allocation; fails closed to recompute on reservation failure; and leaves the staging release paths (SSDPrefixCache.endAdoption/completeStaging, EngineV2Bridge backstops) intact. Without that source, no concrete regression can be cited.
